overview.text: Holy Cross parish’s published feast account commemorates the finding of Christ’s Cross and its elevation before the people. It gives September 14 as the church-calendar feast date; this label does not itself select a civil-calendar equivalent.
overview.reason: Necessary concise account of a modern published explanation; full prose reproduction rights have not been established.

blocks.text: The icon type shows Patriarch Macarius lifting the Cross from the pulpit. Clergy and laypeople gather around him, including Saint Helen; deacons carry candles. The article explains the composition through the Church’s traditional narrative of the Cross’s discovery in Jerusalem.
blocks.reason: Necessary concise account of a modern published explanation; full prose reproduction rights have not been established.

blocks.text: In the published tradition, Helen finds three crosses, a healing identifies Christ’s Cross, and Macarius raises it so the people can see. This is the feast account’s sacred narrative, distinct from the date and provenance of any surviving icon.

blocks.text: The parish reads the feast as the transformation of an instrument of shame into a sign of victory over death. It connects the Cross with the universality of redemption and the contrast between divine and worldly wisdom.
